title: Bram and the Runaway Silver
markdown:
Whoosh. Bang. Clatter. Bram the apprentice wizard bolted upright in his bed. The morning sun usually streamed gently through his window, painting patterns on the floor. Today it bounced crazily off everything. His cozy room was a whirlwind of gleam and glitter. Silver spoons did spectacular loop-de-loops around his desk lamp, clinking like tiny bells. Plump round teapots, usually quite calm, zoomed like miniature silver rockets past his nose, making little toot-toot sounds. And the big proud magic mirror on his wall? It was giggling. A loud tinkling giggle that bounced off the walls. Hee hee hee.

"Crumbs and cauldrons." He bounded out of rumpled covers and tugged his slightly-too-big midnight-blue wizard robe. The air itself sparkled and zoomed with tiny flecks of silver light. Every single silver object in his cozy cottage was alive, gliding, skipping, zooming away as if it had important places to be. A silver sugar bowl did a jig on the bookshelf. A candlestick did a wobbly walk across the rug.

"Bram. Grip, sleepyhead." Clover the talking hedgehog, prickles twitching like antennae, puffed on the floor, batting a runaway thimble with her nose. "You forgot to counter the Glimmer-Gleam polish. Yesterday's brew. I told you it wanted a calming charm."

Bram blinked. "Maybe. It made everything so wonderfully shiny. I forgot the rest." He rubbed his head. "So shiny."

Clover's sigh was deep for her size. "Guests this afternoon. Great Aunt Mildred and her notoriously neat nephew, Bartholomew. They will find flying spoons and a very pinched Bartholomew. The lemon-face. Picture it." Bram could. He shuddered. "Operation Silver Roundup." He puffed his chest.

"More like Operation Do Not Let Bartholomew Dampen the Day," Clover muttered, bead-eyes bright anyway. Prickles ready.

Their first target was a dainty teacup. It zipped past Bram's ear with a cheerful clink, trailing a faint delightful scent of peppermint tea. "After it, Clover." They dashed, his robe flapping like a cape. Clover, much closer to the ground, was surprisingly nimble. Her little legs were a blur, pitter-patter-pitter-patter, as she darted and weaved. "This way, you slippery scallywag." He managed to trap it between two cushions just as it was about to leap onto the mantelpiece. One catch. The shine did not stop.

Next, a whole parade of tiny shining teaspoons marched out the open window, a perfect line, a miniature silver army ready for adventure. "Do not let them escape into the garden." He pointed with his wand and quickly conjured a soft bubbly net of magic. Whoosh. He caught a few of the marching spoons. But the rest, determined to see the world, tumbled and bounced onto the dewy grass, glinting like fallen stars under the morning sky. "This is much harder than it looks." He panted, scrambling outside to grab a spoon before it could bounce away and join the ants. One spoon hid under a daisy. Another pinged off the watering can and made for the herb patch as if mint were a holiday.

Clover nudged a particularly proud oversized serving spoon with her nose. It was much bigger than she was. She was fearless. "It is not about how big they are. It is about catching them with a plan. That mirror, though. It is going to be the trickiest of all. So full of itself."

The mirror floated, showing Bram's flushed face, Clover's snout, a ladybug on the pane. "Give up, little wizard," it boomed, a thousand happy bells. "You cannot catch what you cannot hold. Your guests can admire my shine and forget your dusty corners." It preened.

"Never." A spark of proper defiance. Master Elara's trick. He wiggled fingers, concentrated. "Mirror, mirror, what is the fairest way to stop your spree and bring back the calm?"

The mirror loved fairness. It hesitated. "The fairest way. The absolute fairest. Be still and calm."

"Exactly. And to be still, you belong on your stand." He pointed. "Clover. A gentle nudge."

She scampered the rough plaster, claws finding holds, and shoved with all her hedgehog might. The mirror wobbled, considered, and glided onto its ornate stand with a contented sigh, pleased to have been admired into obedience.

With the mirror captured and behaving, the last of the teapots and spoons lost their zip. They wobbled to a stop, tired, ready to be gathered. Bram and Clover worked quickly now, a blur of focused energy. He scooped the smaller items. She, with surprising strength, pushed the heavier pieces closer. A perfect pair: wizard in a too-big robe, hedgehog with a plan.

A loud clear knock-knock-knock echoed from the front door. Guests. His eyes went wide. Almost tidy. Just a few stray silver buttons near the hearth, gleaming innocently. "Quick, Clover." A final flourish of the wand. Poof. Buttons settled neatly into a small silver dish. He took a deep breath, heart a mix of relief and pure fizz.

Clover's nose twitched, prickles settling. "Close. Not quite a disaster."

The door creaked. Great Aunt Mildred and Bartholomew, he suspiciously speckless. "Good afternoon, Bram," Mildred chirped, bright as a new penny. "Everything seems… surprisingly tidy."

Bartholomew sniffed. "Remarkable. Not a speck. Unexpected."

Bram's grin took his whole face. "Welcome. An active morning. Everything is in its place now." Clover's tiny nod. He did not sit down. The sun still bounced a little on the dish of buttons, and the day, having been caught, was ready to begin again, brighter for having been chased.
